cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Hypnotised – having been put into a state of hypnosis; highly captivated.

p.em: Example: She sat completely hypnotised by the beautiful piano performance.

cosy-blockquote.p: Paradise – an ideal or idyllic place or state; heaven.

p.em: Example: The tropical island felt like a peaceful paradise on earth.

cosy-blockquote.p: Disguise – give a new appearance to hide identity.

p.em: Example: She wore a wig as a clever disguise.

cosy-blockquote.p: Shiver – shake slightly and uncontrollably as a result of being cold, frightened, or excited.

p.em: Example: The cold winter wind made her shiver despite her warm coat.

cosy-blockquote.p: Game – an activity or sport played according to rules, or a deceptive trick.

p.em: Example: He realized his friend was playing a manipulative game with his feelings.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pay – give someone money that is due for work done, or suffer the consequences of an action.

p.em: Example: If you treat people badly, you will eventually have to pay the price.

cosy-blockquote.p: Lonely – sad because one has no friends or company.

p.em: Example: She felt very lonely during her first week living in the big city.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pain – highly distressing physical or emotional sensation.

p.em: Example: Time eventually heals the deep pain of a broken heart.

cosy-blockquote.p: Disappointment – sadness or displeasure caused by the nonfulfillment of one's hopes or expectations.

p.em: Example: Her failing grade was a major disappointment to her parents.
Example: He would gaze at the stars for hours in the backyard.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: There is a big improvement of → Correct: There is a big improvement in my English ((Use 'in' after 'improvement' to express domain.))
Incorrect: It was a great relief of → Correct: It was a great relief to hear the news ((Use 'relief' + infinitive 'to hear'.))
Incorrect: She is in the choir since → Correct: She has been in the choir for three years ((Use present perfect + 'for' to show duration of state.))
